records.text: Comparative bullet lead analysis was primarily used by the FBI until 2004 and abandoned in 2005 because of flawed scientific, statistical, and interpretive validity.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And lo and behold, we find out that the CBLA. The compositional analysis is a discontinued forensic technique that analyzed trace elements, copper, arsenic, in lead to link crime scene bullets to suspects. ... It was primarily used by the FBI from the 1980s until 2004, but it was then abandoned in 2005 due to flawed scientific, statistical, and interpretive validity.

verification.notes: The FBI confirms it conducted bullet-lead examinations from the early 1980s and formally discontinued them in September 2005 after an outside review and internal study. The National Research Council found the analytical instrumentation precise but raised serious limits on interpretation and evidentiary significance. Thus the timing and abandonment are broadly right, but saying the method was abandoned simply because its scientific, statistical, and interpretive validity were all flawed overstates the official findings.

records.text: The FBI is bringing back an already debunked technique so that it can give Erika the evidence she needs to connect the gun to Tyler Robinson.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Bombshell should be on the cover of every mainstream news reporting that the FBI is bringing back an already debunked technique so that they can give Erika (Erika Kirk) the evidence she needs. ... to connect this gun, which hasn't even been fired, to Tyler Robinson.

verification.notes: The March 2026 defense filing supports the narrow fact that the FBI was then conducting a bullet-lead analysis, a type of examination the FBI had discontinued in 2005. No source reviewed supports the claimed purpose of manufacturing evidence for Erika Kirk or establishes any Erika-FBI coordination. The operational premise is supported; the alleged motive and beneficiary are not.

verification.notes: The transcript says the FBI abandoned comparative bullet lead analysis one year after the 2004 National Research Council review. The FBI Laboratory's September 1, 2005 announcement directly confirms that it would no longer conduct bullet-lead examinations after reviewing the NRC recommendations. The statement is accurate as a concise description of the FBI's 2005 discontinuation decision; the release also clarifies that the FBI did not declare every prior report erroneous.
